hero.headline: Penetration Testing — Validate Your Defenses Under Real Attack Conditions
hero.subtitle: Simulate the full attack chain to reveal exploitable weaknesses, validate controls, and prioritize fixes with evidence-based findings and remediation guidance.

whatIs.heading: What is Penetration Testing?
whatIs.body: Penetration testing is more than a scan — it's a controlled cyberattack designed to expose real weaknesses in your environment. At WHITEGUARD, we deliver tailored penetration testing engagements across networks, web/mobile/desktop apps, APIs, wireless, POS, cloud, ITM & ATM, and OT environments. Whether you're meeting compliance, validating new deployments, or securing legacy systems, our certified testers reveal the exploitable paths attackers could take — so you can close them with confidence.

whoNeeds.heading: Who Needs a Penetration Test?
whoNeeds.subtitle: Ideal for security teams, IT leaders, product owners, and compliance officers who need to:
whoNeeds.examples: Short Examples: Startups launching MVPs | SaaS vendors preparing SOC/ISO audits | Banks and fintechs requiring regulatory assurance | Healthcare & MedTech firms protecting PHI | Enterprises validating network and cloud changes

items.title: Web & API Applications
items.description: OWASP Top 10, authentication & session management, business logic, API misuse, SSRF, injection, broken access control.

items.title: Mobile Applications (iOS/Android)
items.description: Local storage, insecure communication, reverse engineering, improper platform usage, API-backed endpoint security.

items.title: Network & Infrastructure
items.description: External perimeter, internal segmentation, VPN, firewalls, exposed services, misconfigurations.

items.title: Cloud & Container Environments
items.description: IAM, misconfigurations (S3, buckets), insecure cloud services, Kubernetes cluster security, IaC (Terraform) review.

items.title: Internal/External Hybrid Tests
items.description: Internal network/lateral movement tests, internal app assessments, endpoint exploitation paths.

items.title: Executive Summary
items.description: Business impact, risk posture, prioritized recommendations for executives and boards.

items.title: Technical Report
items.description: Full findings with PoC, screenshots, exploit steps, affected assets, and CVSS/OWASP mappings.

items.title: Remediation Roadmap
items.description: Prioritized fix list with difficulty, estimated effort, and suggested timelines.

items.title: Retest Report
items.description: Verification of remediation for closed vulnerabilities.

items.title: Developer Pack
items.description: Code snippets, secure configuration examples, and test cases for DevOps.

methodology.heading: Methodology & Process
methodology.subtitle: How We Work — Fast, Transparent, Safe

steps.title: Scope & Rules of Engagement
steps.description: Agree targets, exclusions, test windows, legal sign-off, and emergency contacts.

steps.title: Reconnaissance & Enumeration
steps.description: Passive and active discovery to build an asset inventory and threat surface map.

steps.title: Vulnerability Identification
steps.description: Automated scanning + manual verification to reduce false positives.

steps.title: Exploitation & Impact Validation
steps.description: Attempt safe exploitation to demonstrate impact (PoC) while avoiding destructive tests.

steps.title: Post-Exploitation & Lateral Movement
steps.description: If allowed, identify escalation paths and business-impact scenarios.

steps.title: Reporting & Walkthrough
steps.description: Deliver technical & executive reports; walk your teams through findings.

steps.title: Remediation Support & Retest
steps.description: Validate fixes and issue final closure report.

whenToRun.heading: When Should You Run a PenTest?
items: After major infrastructure change or cloud migration
Following a security incident or suspicious activity
As part of compliance audits (PCI-DSS, FRA, SAMA requirements)
Quarterly/annual assurance program for critical systems
